section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Rates of Change
section_1.content: Briefly define a derivative as the instantaneous slope of a function (velocity from position). Visually represent this as a tangent line sliding along a curve.
section_1.example: A cheetah chasing prey: The derivative represents the cheetah's instantaneous speed at any point in time.

section_2.title: Visualizing Integration as Accumulation
section_2.content: Introduce the integral as the 'area under the curve.' Use a 'filling' animation where a bar graph transforms into a smooth curve, showing the summation of infinite thin rectangles.
section_2.example: The cheetah's GPS tracker logging total distance covered by summing up small 'snapshots' of velocity over time.

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Inverse Connection
section_3.content: Explain that integration is the reverse operation of differentiation. If you accumulate the 'rate of change,' you recover the 'original state.' Use a 'Undo/Redo' button metaphor.
section_3.example: If the speedometer records velocity (derivative), integrating that data perfectly reconstructs the odometer reading (position).

section_4.title: Key Concept: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
section_4.content: Present the visual proof: The rate of change of the area function F(x) is exactly the height of the curve f(x). Show a moving vertical line that 'sweeps' out area.
section_4.example: A robotic arm painting a wall: The rate at which paint covers the wall (area growth) equals the width of the sprayer at that exact point.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude by unifying the concepts. Derivatives 'break down' curves into slopes; Integrals 'build up' curves into areas. They are two sides of the same coin.
section_5.example: A digital music synthesizer: Differentiating the waveform changes its pitch (slope), while integrating it modifies its volume/energy (accumulation).

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)", [
            "The derivative of the area function is f(x).",
            "A vertical line sweeps across the area.",
            "Area growth matches the sprayer's width.",

        # Place graph area

        self.place_in_area(graph, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)

        self.add(line)
        self.play(line.animate.shift(RIGHT * 3), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
